layers.name: Deep Water Base
layers.description: The deepest, underlying color of the water, establishing the overall dark tone and depth.
layers.paintingTip: Start with a generous, diluted wash of Payne's Gray mixed with a touch of Indigo, using a large flat brush (1-inch or wider) to evenly cover the entire water area. Let this layer dry completely.

layers.name: Distant Sky Reflections
layers.description: Broad, lighter blue-grey reflections of the sky on the distant and mid-ground water surface, adding subtle variation.
layers.paintingTip: Apply a lighter wash of Cerulean Blue and a hint of Neutral Tint over the dried base layer, focusing on the upper and middle sections of the water. Use a hake brush or a large round brush (#12) for soft, horizontal strokes, allowing some of the darker base to show through for depth.

layers.name: Warm Sky Reflections
layers.description: Patches of warm, peachy-orange and muted brown tones reflecting from a sunset or sunrise sky, adding atmospheric color.
layers.paintingTip: Introduce soft washes of Permanent Rose mixed with a touch of Cadmium Yellow Light for the lighter areas, and a blend of Burnt Sienna and Raw Umber for the muted brown tones. Use a squirrel mop brush or a soft round brush (#10) for gentle blending, focusing on the upper-left and central-right areas of the water.

layers.name: Bright Vertical Reflection
layers.description: The intense golden-yellow reflection of a distant bright object, likely sunlight on a structure, creating a strong vertical element.
layers.paintingTip: For this dominant reflection, use a concentrated, vibrant mix of Quinacridone Gold and a touch of Raw Sienna. Apply with a flat wash brush (#12) or a medium round brush (#8) in a vertical motion, allowing the edges to remain slightly soft to suggest reflection on water.

layers.name: Mid-tone Water Ripples
layers.description: General, subtle ripple patterns and variations in the mid-ground water surface, adding texture and a sense of movement before the kayak's wake.
layers.paintingTip: Using a slightly thicker mix of Indigo and a hint of Sepia, paint subtle, elongated S-curves and wave patterns across the mid-ground water surface. Use a rigger brush or a fine point round brush (#4) to create these delicate lines, varying pressure for natural unevenness.

layers.name: Kayak Base
layers.description: The primary, vibrant red shape of the kayak, positioned prominently on the water.
layers.paintingTip: Paint the main body of the kayak with a concentrated, pure Cadmium Red. Use a medium round brush (#8) for clean, defined edges and even color application, ensuring the red is opaque enough to stand out against the water.

layers.name: Kayaker Base & Paddle
layers.description: The base colors for the kayaker's hat, life vest, and the paddle, providing the main forms of the person.
layers.paintingTip: For the hat, use a diluted wash of Neutral Tint or a light mix of Payne's Gray. For the life vest, use a solid mix of Ivory Black with a touch of Indigo. Paint the paddle similarly. Use a smaller round brush (#4) for these details, ensuring distinct shapes and avoiding bleeding into the kayak layer.

layers.name: Kayak Shading & Red Accents
layers.description: Adds depth to the kayak with darker red shadows and bright red accents on the kayaker's vest, enhancing realism.
layers.paintingTip: For kayak shading, mix Alizarin Crimson with a tiny bit of Payne's Gray to create a deep, rich red-brown. Apply thinly along the inner edges and under the kayaker with a small round brush (#6). Add vibrant vest accents using clean Cadmium Red with a fine detail brush (#2), ensuring these are crisp.

layers.name: Foreground Dark Water & Wake
layers.description: The darkest and most turbulent water directly surrounding and behind the kayak, emphasizing its movement through the water.
layers.paintingTip: Create the strong wake patterns with a concentrated mix of Indigo and Sepia. Use a flat brush (#6 or #8) to lay down bold, sweeping strokes that capture the energy of the water. Build up layers for depth, ensuring strong contrast with the lighter water around the wake.

layers.name: Final Highlights & Reflections
layers.description: Small, bright highlights on the water, kayak, and paddle, adding sparkle and defining edges for a finishing touch.
layers.paintingTip: Using opaque white gouache or a very light, almost dry-brush stroke of Chinese White, add tiny, sharp highlights. Focus on the edges of the kayak, the paddle blades, and the crests of the water ripples. Use a fine detail brush (#0 or #00) for precision and impact.
